# Pulse task #2691: W20: Qualify the native device platform and full catalog with reproducible quality gates

Operation: d1324fbe0eb43227b7978b75050e60c9
Assignee: PORTALSURFER (Pulse #1, GitHub ID 41680373)

Part of Hex native device roadmap #2661, goal 3, version 0.1. Astra assessment: 17 October 2026.

Goal: define and continuously run honest functional, compatibility, usability and performance acceptance across the full device system.

Deliverables:
- Maintain a registry-driven matrix tying each device/mode to kernel, state/migration, host transport/routing, preset/assets, UI/native, reference and performance results. Current done issues retain finite evidence; unknown/blocked is never counted as full parity.
- Build representative deterministic mixed projects covering 1/16/100 tracks, practical 1/8/16 effect chains, max-supported voices, large IR/sample assets, dense automation/MIDI, racks/sidechains, retained tails, tempo/loop/seek and export. Report admission refusals, not just successful light cases.
- Define hardware budgets after measuring designated macOS arm64: p50/p95/p99/max whole callback, sustained underruns, preparation/apply latency, UI input/paint/focus, peak process/runtime/asset memory and export throughput. Baseline rates 44.1/48/96 kHz and blocks 64/128/256/512 where supported; kernel boundary tests retain 8–192 kHz contracts. Retain raw logs/source/tool/hardware/warm-up/checksums.
- Extend allocation probes to active, edit, handoff, refusal, tail-drain and retirement paths. Run full final-source local CI for implementation PRs and review exact diff; source tests do not substitute for native hardware.
- Coordinate #31 measured reference methodology, #29 accessibility, #2108/#2226 runtime density, #2164 chase, #2388 listening, #2389 export performance and #2650 streaming export. User runs native interaction/listening checklist under current AGENTS policy.
- Include authoring acceptance: two new device classes integrated via documented host-independent DSP/UI APIs with no storage/engine/audio device-ID branches.

Acceptance: platform slices qualify as they land. Final goal closure requires every pinned manual/installed-overlay entry's finite functional acceptance, explicit native/reference evidence status, no unresolved correctness/loss-of-work bugs and measured supported workload limits. No global “blazing fast” or exact-sound-parity claim from short microbenchmarks. W12–W19 results are required for full catalog closure, but this issue starts now to shape budgets and harnesses.

Sources: docs/performance.md, local-ci.md, test-builds.md, AGENTS.md and current allocation/PCM/GPUI suites. Keep ordinary planning todo until implementation is explicitly started.

Planning workstream: split implementation into focused PRs as work begins. Related canonical tickets: #29, #31, #2108, #2226, #2164, #2388, #2389, #2650. Preserve their current scope, versions, status and PR history. Dependency edges order the enabling contracts; downstream production proof is qualified incrementally under W20.
